thread.title: Microsoft shares surge as Morgan Stanley note teases trillion-dollar company track

author: Wallace Witkowski
title: Microsoft shares surge as Morgan Stanley note teases trillion-dollar company track
text:
In recent discussions about companies that are on track to become trillion-dollar behemoths, the two names that most commonly come up are Apple Inc. and Amazon.com Inc., but Morgan Stanley is throwing another contender into the ring: Microsoft Corp.
Microsoft MSFT, +7.57% shares rallied 7.6% to close at $93.78 Monday for their largest one-day percentage gain since October 2015, after hitting an intraday high Monday of $94. Microsoft shares reached an all-time high of $97.24 on March 1.
With an overweight rating Monday, Morgan Stanley analyst Keith Weiss forecast Wall Street’s most bullish price target at $130 a share on Microsoft, which if it were achieved at 7.7 billion shares outstanding would give Microsoft a market cap of $1.001 trillion. That road to $1 trillion is supported by the ramping up of Microsoft’s public cloud service Azure, improving margins and the tech company’s existing customer base, Weiss said. 
Currently, Microsoft has a market cap of $716.6 billion, compared with Apple AAPL, +4.75% at $868.16 billion, Amazon AMZN, +4.03% at $742.58 billion and Alphabet Inc. GOOG, +3.10% GOOGL, +2.68% at $718.2 billion. 
Weiss notes:
A Public Cloud solution spanning from core Infrastructure Services (e.g. compute, storage), to compelling Platform-as-a-Service capabilities (e.g. data, identity, analytics, machine learning), and up the stack to the application layer (e.g. productivity apps, front office apps, core financials) differentiates the Microsoft Public Cloud offering from cloud giants Amazon and Google. However, it is the combination of these Public Cloud assets with pre-existing enterprise assets, including; a large existing customer base, expansive direct and indirect distribution channel, over 6+ million .Net developers and a suite of strong on-premise technology that likely drives continuing share gains over the next three years.
Weiss, who considers Microsoft his top-pick stock, said he expects Microsoft’s public cloud adoption to grow to 44% of workloads in the next three years from its current 21% share. 
Of the 34 analysts who cover Microsoft, 26 have buy or overweight ratings, seven have hold ratings, and one has a sell rating, with an average price target of $104.70. The next highest price target is Deutsche Bank at $120 a share.
